title: 3.5a questions and comments
body:
### Ask or discuss any quick questions about 3.5a here please.

**Do not use this issue for bug reports, they will be ignored** - please open a new issue with full information, see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**[The 3.5a CHANGES file is here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.5a/CHANGES).**

This is a bug fix release for 3.5, please also see this issue for the 3.5 release: https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4136. The new changes in 3.5a are:

- Restore the `grey` colour name.

- Revert to using `/bin/sh` for `#()`, `run-shell` and `if-shell` - only popups change to use `default-shell`.

- Correct the sequences emitted for Shift keys and `C-BSpace` with extended keys enabled.

Please also note that 3.5 changes the way tmux represents keys, so some keys that were previously the same are now different. For example:

   - `C-A` and `C-a`, `C-B` and `C-b` and so on;
   - `C-i` and `Tab`;
   - `C-m` and `Enter`;
   - `C-@` and `C-Space`;
   - `C-Enter` and `Enter`;
   - `C-BTab` and `C-S-Tab`.
 
Any bindings for these keys will need to be changed in `.tmux.conf` for 3.5a.

Note that a fix in 3.5 and 3.5a to correctly set `SHELL` for `run-shell` and `if-shell` reveals a bug in the `tmux-sensible` script, causing it to set `default-shell` to `/bin/sh`. This can be worked around by adding this to `.tmux.conf` after the `tmux-sensible` script is invoked:
~~~~
set -gu default-command
set -g default-shell "$SHELL"
~~~~

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
For anyone who had a config like this:

```
bind -r C-[ previous-window
bind -r C-] next-window
```

You need to change it to:

```
bind -r Escape previous-window
bind -r C-] next-window
```

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
I'm going from Tmux 2.7 to Tmux 3.5a. Previously, I used to be able to do `Leader Key + Esc + Direction Arrow` to resize panes in tmux and as far as I know this didn't require any additional configuration (though I set it up many moons ago, so I may be misremembering). It appears on 3.5a this keyboard shortcut does not work and after spending a few hours trying to find the incantation to restore the behavior I am at a loss. 

I was hoping to appeal to those more versed in tmux in order to figure out how I can restore my workflow. Thanks in advance for any assistance for all the work you do and I appreciate the software!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: You were probably managing to press Esc and the arrow keys within the default escape time of 500 milliseconds, this has now been reduced. Try `set -s escape-time 500`.

comments.author: participant14

This is just a note for changes in 3.5, not 3.5a.

Using (the opt-in) `--enable-jemalloc` will create unportable binaries. jemalloc has been a particular issue on arm64 devices which do not use a 4k page size. Please be aware that tmux users may report related issues. https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/issues/467

comments.author: participant21
comments.body:
Terminal emulator maintainer here! Hi! I'm unsure of the etiquette on this repository, so I apologize if I've done something wrong and should have made a separate issue. This is a comment on 3.5a.

It's about `escape-time`. I've collapsed it so that it doesn't clutter up the repo. It's medium length and uses em-dashes, but I promise I didn't use a LLM to generate it.

<details>
<summary>Dustin rants about `escape-time`</summary>

We're getting a lot of user reports of broken escape sequences including those in bracketed paste--especially over network links--which point back to the new value of `escape-time` (10ms, introduced in 2e9d7ebf15615b51b014a12de03b0e5483aadf99 re #3844) being quite low.

I'm not sure what it is about our stack (windows, winsock, windows port of openssh, etc.) that triggers this more often, but... from a raw numbers perspective, I can't bring myself to agree with 10ms being a reasonable default.

I suspect that a lot of folks use tmux over a network.

Assuming a network with no additional latency, a 10ms gap is only sufficient to handle fragmented escape sequence reassembly at a distance of ~3000km. Considering that most networks have significantly more than 0ms additional latency, that range drops pretty quickly...

The fastest typist in the world (as of 2025? I think?) seems to be able to type 30 characters per second... with a delay of only 33ms between them. I understand that that person may want to press <kbd>Esc</kbd> as quickly as possible and then move on to their next character, but I am not sure that it's conceivable that that could happen within that 33ms budget.

Bringing the default up to 50ms increases the no-latency range to ~14,000km and I would love to meet the typist for whom that is an issue. 🙂 

Cross-linking: this was fixed for palette and DA1/2 reports in https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/e6bac234dbfbbd8709ac91f40dc9788e09daa028 and https://github.com/tmux/tmux/commit/cfb906a0ceb18846ac52561c5def88d155c5e54b.

Alternate solution: perhaps extending the escape time during bracketed paste would also work? It seems like adding a lot of workarounds for a bug that could be fixed more comprehensively... though it does allow users to set `escape-time` to however short they want and not risk breaking anything further!

</details>

All the configuration made in home.nix under programs.tmux ends up in  ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf like I think it should. comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Right but the default for tmux is to try `/etc/tmux.conf:~/.tmux.conf:$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tmux/tmux.conf:~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` and since it isn't finding `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` either that file doesn't actually exist or someone changed the configuration when they built tmux so it isn't checked.

comments.author: participant23
comments.body:
Since
1. most of the configuration is loaded on session startup
2.  /etc/tmux.conf and ~/.tmux.conf do not exist
3.  ~.config/tmux/tmux.conf exists and contains all the configuration it is supposed to contain
4. disabling plugins removes them from the said config file and results in extraConfig getting sourced automatically on session startup

I'm inclined to believe this issue has to do with the ordering of the config sections by home manager options.
